title: V1 magnetics heating at high load

takeaway.text: The V1 thermal image shows a 102.9 °C surface maximum near the magnetics at the labeled 20 V, 4.7 A condition.

visual.layout: Place the complete original thermal image prominently at left, preserving its aspect ratio, camera markers, scale and embedded labels. Place the large temperature callout, its label, the test condition and the short observation in a clear right-hand column. The Results label follows the deck style.
visual.image_handling: Retain the original 240 × 307 pixel asset intact; do not interpolate into a replacement image, crop, retouch or add a component-identifying pointer. Scaling the original asset in the presentation is permitted.
visual.embedded_camera_annotations: The red 102.9 °C camera marker is the maximum. The two 27.9 °C readings are the cursor/display reading, 25.2 °C is a reference marker and e=0.95 is the camera emissivity setting. The lower marker is not labeled as ambient.

speaker_notes: The thermal image shows how strongly the V1 hardware heated at the higher load setting. At the labeled 20 volts and 4.7 amperes, the camera recorded a maximum surface temperature of 102.9 degrees Celsius near the magnetics. The image is a surface-temperature snapshot; no stabilized temperature history was recorded. The heating made the thermal design a practical limit.
transition: During later V2 operation, an external tank inductor also became hot and was removed as part of a tank change.

facts: Image #1 identifies a maximum surface reading; the exact component and winding/core location of the maximum are not established. The user's identification is the magnetics region.
The 20 V and 4.7 A are the labeled condition, not a measured 94 W delivered power; the separate 79.89 W result is not assigned to this image.
The temperature is neither a junction reading nor a claim of equilibrium. The image retains all original camera labels and the original pixel data.
The later V2 inductor observation is distinct; the thermal image is not claimed to show that inductor or to be a matched V1/V2 test.
